title: “Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating…
content: “Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world. Ānanda, thus a monk is an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge.”

title: “And how, good sirs, is one not defiled by sensual lust? Here, good sirs, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is…
content: “And how, good sirs, is one not defiled by sensual lust? Here, good sirs, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he is not attached to agreeable forms nor repelled by disagreeable forms. He dwells with bodily mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. When he tastes a flavor with the tongue … When he cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, he is not attached to agreeable phenomena nor repelled by disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with bodily mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He knows as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Here, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are abandoned without remainder. This, good sirs, is called a monk who is not defiled by sensual lust regarding forms … regarding tastes … regarding phenomena. A monk living thus, good sirs, if Māra approaches him through the eye, Māra does not gain an opportunity, Māra does not gain an object. If Māra approaches him through the tongue … through the mind, Māra does not gain an opportunity, Māra does not gain an object.”

title: “Ānanda, he reflects: ‘Those low, vulgar, worldly, ignoble thoughts that are not connected with the goal and do not lead to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace,…
content: “Ānanda, he reflects: ‘Those low, vulgar, worldly, ignoble thoughts that are not connected with the goal and do not lead to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna — such as sensual thoughts, ill-will thoughts, harmfulness thoughts — I will not think those thoughts.’ In this way, he is clearly aware of that.”

title: The hair is curled in seven rings, The eyes are rubbed with collyrium and rouge — Enough to fool a fool, But not one who…
content:
The hair is curled in seven rings,
The eyes are rubbed with collyrium and rouge —
Enough to fool a fool,
But not one who seeks the far shore.

title: “And how, Mahānāma, does a noble disciple guard the sense faculties? Here, Mahānāma, when a noble disciple sees a form with the eye, he does…
content: “And how, Mahānāma, does a noble disciple guard the sense faculties? Here, Mahānāma, when a noble disciple sees a form with the eye, he does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise—he restrains that cause, guards the eye, practices restraint of the eye. When the ear hears a sound … nose smells an odor … tongue tastes a flavor … body feels a touch … mind cognizes phenomena, he does not grasp the general feature, does not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise—he restrains that cause, guards the mind, practices restraint of the mind. Thus, Mahānāma, a noble disciple guards the sense faculties.”

title: “Monks, if anyone says: ‘Māra’s complete snare’ — he would speak rightly of women. Indeed, women are ‘Māra’s complete snare.’”
content: “Monks, if anyone says: ‘Māra’s complete snare’ — he would speak rightly of women. Indeed, women are ‘Māra’s complete snare.’”

title: “One who does not go too far, Nor lag behind, Having overcome all this unreality — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like…
content:
“One who does not go too far,
Nor lag behind,
Having overcome all this unreality —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who does not go too far,
Nor lag behind,
Knowing that all this is unreality —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who does not go too far,
Nor lag behind,
Free from greed, free from hatred,
Free from delusion —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

title: - “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?” - “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for…
content:
- “Venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
- “Friend, I know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings.”
- “But how, venerable sir, do you know the release, the escape, the seclusion for beings?”
The destruction of delight in renewed existence,
The cessation of perception and consciousness,
The stilling of feelings —
Thus, friend, I know the release,
The escape and seclusion
For all kinds of beings.

title: Elder Raṭṭhapāla: Behold this decorated image — A heap of wounds, a collection of sores, Diseased, full of lustful thoughts, Nothing stable or permanent here.…
content:
Elder Raṭṭhapāla:

Behold this decorated image —
A heap of wounds, a collection of sores,
Diseased, full of lustful thoughts,
Nothing stable or permanent here.

Behold this adorned appearance,
With jewels and earrings —
A skeleton covered by skin,
Made beautiful by clothes.

The feet are painted with lac and dye,
The face is smeared with powder and paste —
Enough to fool a fool,
Not one who seeks enlightenment.

The hair is curled in eight rings,
The eyes are rubbed with collyrium and rouge —
Enough to fool a fool,
Not one who seeks enlightenment.

Like a newly painted medicine box,
This foul body is adorned —
Enough to fool a fool,
Not one who seeks enlightenment.

The hunter set his trap and snare —
The wise deer does not touch the snare.
Having eaten the bait, we go away,
Leaving the trapper to mourn.

The hunter’s trap is cut —
The wise deer does not touch the snare.
Having eaten the bait, we go away,
Leaving the trapper to grieve.

title: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should…
content: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling … perception … formations … consciousness there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all consciousness should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Rādha, knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding this conscious body and all external signs, there is no ‘I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit.’”
